title: Native Weil compact structure tensor comparison
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Use the actual categories $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(T_0)\subset D(\mathcal W_T)$, full subcategories with bounded constructible cohomology, and the actual equivariant derived operations of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], with the tensor, internal Hom and coefficient unit $\mathbf1_0$ of [def-sf-derived-weil-category-and-operations]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated, quasi-compact, locally finite-type $k_0$-morphism between separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes. Put $s_0=\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ and let $a_{T,0}:T_0\to s_0$ be the structure morphisms for $T=X,Y$, so $a_{Y,0}f_0=a_{X,0}$. Write $F=Rf_{0!}$ and $A_T=Ra_{T,0!}$ for the actual compact-support functors, and let $f^*$ be actual derived module pullback. For every $M\in\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(X_0)$ and $L\in\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(Y_0)$, all of $FM$, $f^*L$, $FM\otimes^L_{B_Y}L$, and $M\otimes^L_{B_X}f^*L$ belong to the indicated bounded constructible full subcategories. There is an isomorphism in $\mathrm{WC}^{\mathrm{der}}(s_0)$
$$e_{M,L}:A_Y(FM\otimes^L_{B_Y}L)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X(M\otimes^L_{B_X}f^*L),$$
natural in $M,L$. More precisely, let $\pi_{M,L}:FM\otimes^L L\xrightarrow{\sim}F(M\otimes^Lf^*L)$ be the actual compactification projection isomorphism, and let $\gamma:A_X\xrightarrow{\sim}A_YF$ be the native compact-support composition isomorphism. Then
$$e_{M,L}=\gamma_{M\otimes^Lf^*L}^{-1}\circ A_Y(\pi_{M,L}).$$
For the coefficient unit $\mathbf1_0$, precomposition with $e_{M,L}^{-1}$ gives a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{s_0}(A_Y(FM\otimes^L L),\mathbf1_0)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{s_0}(A_X(M\otimes^Lf^*L),\mathbf1_0),\qquad h\longmapsto h\circ e_{M,L}^{-1},$$
whose inverse is $h'\mapsto h'\circ e_{M,L}$ and which is natural contravariantly in $M,L$.

proof.text: Finite type means quasi-compact and locally finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], so $f_0,a_{X,0},a_{Y,0}$ are separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], quasi-compact and locally of finite type, as the projection, pullback and compact-support statements require. These also need the schemes $Y_0,s_0$ quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. $Y_0$ is a finite union of $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$, $B_i$ finitely generated over $k_0$, hence Noetherian; so every open of $Y_0$, in particular each diagonal inverse image of an affine open of $Y_0\times_{\mathbf Z}Y_0$, is quasi-compact. $s_0$ is a point.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-native-weil-shriek-triangulated] to $f_0$, $a_{X,0}$ and $a_{Y,0}$: $F,A_X,A_Y$ carry bounded constructible objects to bounded constructible objects. By [lem-sf-native-weil-pullback-star-preservation], $f^*L$ belongs to the indicated category on $X_0$. Apply [lem-sf-derived-weil-tensor-hom-adjunction] to $(FM,L)$ on $Y_0$ and to $(M,f^*L)$ on $X_0$. This gives exactly both tensor-domain assertions, and makes $F(M\otimes^Lf^*L)$ and both structure pushforwards legitimate objects of the stated full subcategories.

proof.text: Put $K=M\otimes^Lf^*L$ and $P=FM\otimes^LL$. The natural compactification projection isomorphism $\pi:P\xrightarrow{\sim}FK$ is [lem-sf-derived-weil-compact-projection-formula]. Apply [lem-sf-native-weil-shriek-composition] to $X_0\xrightarrow{f_0}Y_0\xrightarrow{a_{Y,0}}s_0$. Since $a_{Y,0}f_0=a_{X,0}$, this gives the native functor isomorphism $\gamma:A_X\xrightarrow{\sim}A_YF$. Define $e=\gamma_K^{-1}\circ A_Y(\pi):A_YP\to A_XK$. Its inverse is $A_Y(\pi^{-1})\circ\gamma_K$; the two composites are identities by functoriality and the inverse identities for $\pi$ and $\gamma_K$. All arrows are in the native Weil categories.

proof.text: For $u:M\to M\prime$ and $v:L\to L\prime$, write $p=Fu\otimes v:P\to P\prime$ and $q=u\otimes f^*v:K\to K\prime$. Naturality of the projection isomorphism [lem-sf-derived-weil-compact-projection-formula] gives $Fq\circ\pi=\pi\prime\circ p$. Naturality of the functor isomorphism [lem-sf-native-weil-shriek-composition] gives $A_Y(Fq)\circ\gamma_K=\gamma_{K\prime}\circ A_X(q)$. Substitution yields $A_X(q)\circ e=e\prime\circ A_Y(p)$, proving naturality of $e$ in both variables. Inverting this equation yields $e\prime^{-1}\circ A_X(q)=A_Y(p)\circ e^{-1}$.

proof.text: Use the coefficient unit $\mathbf1_0$ defined in [def-sf-derived-weil-category-and-operations]. Set $H(h)=h\circ e^{-1}$ and $J(h\prime)=h\prime\circ e$. Then $J(H(h))=h\circ e^{-1}\circ e=h$ and $H(J(h\prime))=h\prime\circ e\circ e^{-1}=h\prime$, so these are inverse bijections on the displayed Hom sets. For the maps $p,q$ of the preceding step and $h\prime:A_YP\prime\to\mathbf1_0$, its final equation gives $(h\prime\circ A_Y(p))\circ e^{-1}=(h\prime\circ e\prime^{-1})\circ A_X(q)$. This is exactly the contravariant naturality square for $H$ in $(M,L)$. The inverse bijection is natural as well, by composing this equality with the mutually inverse maps $H,J$.
